metrics.topology: Özgen: two lobes joined at the nose, SEPARATED by a stable gap at high Re; pyMack: CONNECTED band (gap filled by marginal instability)
metrics.headline: 2nd-mode cutoff agrees (2%); pyMack fills the inter-mode stable gap Özgen shows (connected vs separated) — 2nd-onset/1st-cutoff inner branches have no pyMack c_i=0 counterpart

verdict_reason: Re-judged with the discrete-mode extractor. The dominant SECOND (Mack) mode CUTOFF branch agrees with Özgen to 2% (the transition-relevant 2nd-mode neutral curve, rising to alpha~0.13-0.20). However, Özgen's M7 panel shows the first and second modes as TWO lobes that join at the nose but are SEPARATED by a stable gap at high Re; pyMack instead predicts a CONNECTED band — it is (marginally) unstable in the inter-mode gap that Özgen shows stable. So Özgen's two inner c_i=0 boundaries (2nd-mode onset ~0.11-0.13, 1st-mode cutoff ~0.08-0.09) have NO pyMack c_i=0 counterpart, and the nearest-crossing match for those reads 59%/92%. The 1st-mode low-alpha onset roughly tracks (31%, rel-err inflated by the tiny denominator). This gap-fill is a marginal over-prediction that grows with Mach (M4/M6 keep the modes separated and match all four branches; by M7-10 the gap narrows and pyMack bridges it) — a coherent marginal-instability formulation difference, not a 2nd-mode-curve error. Honest verdict: 'acceptable' — the dominant 2nd-mode neutral curve agrees (2%), with a documented connected-vs-separated topology difference in the weak inter-mode region.
